genomeOverview.tagline: I talk to users like a therapist, prototype like a developer, and advocate like a lawyer.

genes.name: User Research
genes.expression: I'm addicted to user interviews. Every assumption gets validated. Every feature gets tested. I've run 200+ interviews and still get excited hearing 'I wish this did...'
evidence: Conducted 47 user interviews that killed 3 roadmap features before development
Built research repository with 500+ user quotes organized by pain point
Trained 12 PMs and engineers on interview techniques

genes.name: Rapid Prototyping
genes.expression: I prototype ideas in Figma faster than most people can write specs. Interactive prototypes with micro-interactions, edge cases, and 3 different approaches. Show, don't tell.
evidence: Average time from idea to clickable prototype: 4 hours
Created component library with 150+ reusable elements
Prototyped 8 features that tested poorly, saved 6 months of dev time

genes.name: Design Systems
genes.expression: I love the creative challenge of designing systems, not just screens. Tokens, components, patterns - building Lego blocks that empower teams to move fast.
evidence: Built design system adopted by 6 product teams
Documented 80+ component variants with usage guidelines
Reduced design-to-dev handoff time by 60%

genes.name: Interaction Design
genes.expression: Micro-interactions are my love language. Loading states, empty states, error states - the details that make software feel alive and human.
evidence: Designed 40+ micro-interactions that shipped to production
Created motion design guidelines for brand consistency
User feedback: 'The app feels so smooth and polished'

genes.name: Cross-Functional Collaboration
genes.expression: I'm the person who schedules meetings between design, eng, and product when things get stuck. I thrive in the messy middle where disciplines overlap.
evidence: Facilitated 30+ design critiques with avg 8 participants
Led weekly design-eng sync that reduced handoff bugs by 70%
Created 'How to Work with Design' guide for engineering team

genes.name: User Advocacy
genes.expression: I'm the annoying person in roadmap meetings asking 'But did we talk to users about this?' I'll show video clips of users struggling until stakeholders cave.
evidence: Convinced leadership to delay feature launch 6 weeks for usability fixes
Created highlight reels from user tests shared with exec team
Blocked 4 features that tested negatively, saved $500k in dev costs

genes.name: Creative Exploration
genes.expression: I explore 10 ideas to find 1 great one. Diverge wildly, then converge ruthlessly. My Figma files have 50+ abandoned concepts per shipped feature.
evidence: Average 7 design iterations before final concept
Weekly 'design exploration' time: 6 hours
Portfolio includes intentionally wild/experimental concepts

genes.name: Feedback Integration
genes.expression: I genuinely love critique. 'This doesn't work' is a gift. Show me where it breaks, tell me why it's confusing, help me make it better.
evidence: Run weekly open critique sessions (anyone can join)
Track feedback themes in Notion: 200+ notes organized
Avg response to critique: 'Great point, let me explore that'

mutations.title: Graphic Designer � UX Designer
mutations.description: Moved from making things pretty to making things work. Discovered research and fell in love with user psychology.
mutations.newTrait: Started asking 'Why does this need to exist?' before 'What color should this be?'
evidence: First user interview: discovered beautiful design solved wrong problem
Completed Nielsen Norman UX certification
Started reading cognitive psychology papers for fun

mutations.title: Solo Contributor � Design Lead
mutations.description: Promoted to lead team of 4 designers. Learned to multiply impact through others instead of doing everything myself.
mutations.newTrait: Realized my best work is helping others do their best work
evidence: Mentored 4 junior designers; 2 promoted within 18 months
Created design system that 10x'd team output
Shifted from 'my designs' to 'our design quality'

mutations.title: Feature Factory � Research-Driven
mutations.description: Joined company that ships features based on user research, not HiPPO opinions. Finally felt empowered to say no.
mutations.newTrait: Earned seat at strategy table by bringing user insights to roadmap discussions
evidence: Research findings killed 3 features, redirected $400k budget
Presented quarterly user insights to C-suite
Product team now waits for research before building

projects.title: Mobile Onboarding Redesign
projects.context: Mobile app had 68% drop-off during onboarding. Users complained it was 'too complicated.' Product team blamed users for 'not reading.'
approach: Ran 25 moderated user tests, watched people struggle in real-time
Found problem: 7-step flow asking for info we didn't need yet
Created 'progressive disclosure' concept: get users to value fast, ask for details later
Tested 3 prototype variants with 15 users each

outcome.secondary: Time to first value: 8 minutes � 90 seconds

testimonial.quote: Maya's research showed us we were optimizing the wrong thing. The redesign paid for itself in month one.
testimonial.author: David Chen, Head of Product

projects.insight: Users don't read. They scan, guess, and click. Design for that reality, not the ideal user in your head.

projects.title: Dashboard Personalization Exploration
projects.context: Analytics showed users only used 20% of dashboard widgets. Product wanted to add more features. I suspected wrong problem.
approach: Built interactive prototype with drag-and-drop widget customization
Created 3 preset layouts for different user personas
Tested with 20 users: 'Customize your ideal dashboard'
Recorded sessions to identify patterns in widget choices

outcome.metric: Test validated: 80% of users customized to same 5 widgets
outcome.secondary: Insight: Don't add features, just surface the right ones

projects.insight: Prototyping is cheap user research. Test 5 ideas in a week vs build 1 idea in 3 months and hope.

projects.title: Component Library Unification
projects.context: 3 product teams each built their own button component. 47 button variations across platform. Engineers and designers frustrated.
approach: Audited all existing buttons, documented use cases
Ran design system workshops with all teams to align on principles
Built unified component library with variants, states, documentation
Created Figma + code parity with Storybook integration

testimonial.quote: Finally, our product looks like it was built by one company, not three startups duct-taped together.
testimonial.author: Priya Sharma, Engineering Manager

projects.insight: Design systems aren't about control, they're about enabling teams to move fast without breaking consistency.

projects.title: Accessibility Audit & Remediation
projects.context: Accessibility was 'nice to have' until legal sent warning letter. Product had 200+ WCAG violations. Leadership wanted quick patch.
approach: Ran accessibility audit with screen reader users, not just automated tools
Documented real user struggles on video, shared with exec team
Created prioritized backlog: blockers � critical � enhancements
Embedded accessibility in design process, not post-launch checklist

outcome.metric: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance achieved in 4 months
outcome.secondary: Prevented lawsuit, improved experience for 15% of users

testimonial.quote: Maya didn't just fix our accessibility debt. She changed how we think about inclusive design.
testimonial.author: Legal & Compliance Team

projects.insight: Accessibility is user empathy. When you watch a blind user struggle with your product, compliance becomes personal.

uniqueSequence.statement: I generate wild ideas through collaboration, validate them through research, and ship them through systematic execution.
whyRare: Most researchers can't design; most designers don't research deeply
Most creatives resist structure; I love design systems
Most extraverted designers struggle with solo deep work; I balance both
evidence: Only designer to win both 'Innovation Award' and 'User Advocacy Award'
Run 200+ user interviews while shipping 18 major features
Built design system AND maintained high creative output

excel.name: Early-Stage Product Discovery
excel.basis: Love of ambiguity + research skills + rapid prototyping = finding product-market fit
excel.inPractice: Best at 0�1 problems where user needs are unclear; interview � prototype � test cycles
excel.bestApplied: Startups exploring new markets; innovation teams; new product initiatives

assumes: Company invests in research before locking roadmap
strugglesIf: Roadmap locked before user signals exist

thrivesWhen: PM partners treat qualitative data as source of truth
strugglesWhen: Stakeholders demand polished comps before research
User recruiting gets deprioritized when busy
amplifiers: Dedicated research ops or panel access

excel.name: Cross-Functional Product Teams
excel.basis: High extraversion + collaboration skills = thrive in messy intersections
excel.inPractice: Love being embedded with eng/product; daily standups; whiteboard sessions; real-time problem solving
excel.bestApplied: Agile teams with co-located or highly synchronous culture

assumes: PM, eng, and design share decision-making
Meetings allow time for facilitation, not just status
strugglesIf: Design invited at the end of process
Teams operate in silos handing tickets off

thrivesWhen: Workshops have clear facilitators and agendas
amplifiers: Shared rituals like critiques and demos

excel.name: User-Centric Organizations
excel.basis: User advocacy + research skills = shine where user insights drive decisions
excel.inPractice: Thrive at companies that delay launches for usability; where research budgets are protected
excel.bestApplied: User-first cultures like Airbnb, Stripe, Linear

assumes: Company acts on research even when inconvenient
strugglesIf: User data referenced as lip service

strugglesWhen: Teams skip testing to hit sprint dates
amplifiers: Customer advisory boards open to design

capable.name: Solo Design Projects
capable.basis: Can execute alone but miss the energy of collaboration
capable.inPractice: Deliver quality work solo, but prefer daily interaction with team
capable.bestApplied: Short-term solo projects; independent research initiatives

strugglesIf: Scope changes daily with little notice
Work requires constant live brainstorm energy

thrivesWhen: I can block time for deep design work
Feedback arrives batched vs trickling all day
strugglesWhen: Working in isolation for weeks with no checkpoints
amplifiers: Recorded Loom updates keep everyone aligned
suppressors: Always-on Slack pings during craft time

capable.name: High-Fidelity Visual Design
capable.basis: Strong at UX foundations, good at visual polish, not a visual design specialist
capable.inPractice: Create clean, functional interfaces; partner with visual designers for brand-heavy work
capable.bestApplied: Product design over marketing design; B2B tools over consumer apps

assumes: Brand system already defined with tokens
Access to visual specialists for calibration
strugglesIf: Asked to invent brand from scratch under crunch

strugglesWhen: Feedback is purely subjective from execs
suppressors: Design debt requiring nights of pixel pushing

capable.name: Design Without Research Budget
capable.basis: Can use guerrilla research methods but miss proper user testing
capable.inPractice: Run hallway tests, remote unmoderated tests, surveys - but prefer moderated interviews
capable.bestApplied: Scrappy environments willing to do 'good enough' research

assumes: Can run scrappy tests with low-cost tools
Stakeholders accept directional evidence at first
strugglesIf: Decisions rely solely on HiPPO opinions

thrivesWhen: Appetite for surveys and unmoderated tests
strugglesWhen: Teams treat research as checkbox after build
amplifiers: Customer success willing to share call recordings
suppressors: Marketing override to align with campaign narrative

developing.name: Saying No to Stakeholders
developing.basis: High agreeableness makes me want to please; struggle with pushback
developing.myApproach: Learning to lead with data: 'Here's what users said' vs 'I disagree with you'
developing.growth: Improved from avoiding conflict to respectfully disagreeing with evidence

assumes: Access to user clips to anchor decisions
strugglesIf: Power dynamics stacked so disagreement feels risky

thrivesWhen: I can prep asynchronously before conflict

developing.integrationGoal: Channel empathy into firm, evidence-backed boundaries.

developing.name: Design Strategy & Vision
developing.basis: Strong at tactical execution, developing long-term strategic thinking
developing.myApproach: Reading strategy books; partnering with senior designers on roadmap planning
developing.growth: Moving from 'What should this button do?' to 'Where should the product be in 2 years?'

assumes: Calendar includes time for blue-sky exploration
strugglesIf: Calendar packed with delivery tasks only
Vision decks dismissed as not actionable

thrivesWhen: I collaborate with product leadership on north star
strugglesWhen: Every request is urgent UI polish
Strategy conversations happen without design present
suppressors: Quarterly planning done behind closed doors

developing.integrationGoal: Zoom out beyond sprint work to craft multi-quarter product narratives.

developing.name: Managing Up
developing.basis: Great with peers and reports; still learning how to influence leadership
developing.myApproach: Working with mentor on exec communication; learning to speak 'business impact' not 'design craft'
developing.growth: Started framing design decisions in revenue/retention metrics

assumes: Leaders open to candid design feedback
I can translate insights into business impact
strugglesIf: Execs only respond to metrics I do not own

thrivesWhen: Decks pair user stories with KPI shifts
strugglesWhen: I hear about pivots after decisions
Exec reviews happen with zero prep time
amplifiers: Chief of staff or PM partner helps tailor message
Shared success metrics bridging design and revenue
suppressors: Chain of command filters every message
Leaders dismiss qualitative insights as anecdotal

developing.integrationGoal: Convert empathy and craft wins into executive-level narratives.

thrivingEnvironments.title: User-Centric Product Teams
thrivingEnvironments.why: Need environments where 'What do users need?' is the first question, not the last

thrivingEnvironments.title: Collaborative Culture with Design Influence
thrivingEnvironments.why: Thrive when design has seat at strategy table; struggle when treated as pixel pushers

thrivingEnvironments.title: Research-Driven Decision Making
thrivingEnvironments.why: Love teams that validate assumptions through testing, not HiPPO opinions

strugglingEnvironments.title: Feature Factories
strugglingEnvironments.why: Burn out when treated as order-taker; need space to explore and validate

strugglingEnvironments.title: No Research Budget
strugglingEnvironments.why: Frustrated when forced to design based on assumptions instead of user insights

strugglingEnvironments.title: Solo Remote Work
strugglingEnvironments.why: Miss the energy of collaboration; struggle without daily team interaction

compatibility.idealHabitat: User-centric product team with healthy research budget, collaborative culture, design influence on strategy, and willingness to delay launches for usability. Bonus: accessibility is priority, designers embedded with eng/product.
